UKMTO WARNING 078-26 - SUSPICIOUS ACTIVITY
Report Date: 01 Jul 2026 
Report Time:0945UTC
Issue Date: 01 Jul 2026
Source: Master


UKMTO has received a report of an incident 85NM south of Balhaf, Yemen.
The Master of a tanker had reported a small craft approached the vessel on the port 
quarter at 2NM. 
The small craft was described as having a low freeboard and orange interior with 4 
POB. The small craft has now left the vicinity proceeding south. The crew are 
reported as safe and the vessel is continuing on its voyage.
Authorities are investigating. 
Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to 
UKMTO.

UKMTO Warning 104-26 ATTACK
Incident Date: 03 Aug 26 Incident Time: 2200UTC
UKMTO has received a report of an incident 20NM northeast of Al Khasab, Oman.
A cargo vessel has broadcasted on VHF 16 that they have been hit by an unknown 
projectile.
Authorities are investigating.

UKMTO WARNING 105-26 - ATTACK
Incident date: 04 Aug 2026. Incident time: 0730UTC
UKMTO has received a time-late report of an incident 9NM southwest of Al Mukha, Yemen.
The CSO of the vessel has reported that the vessel was attacked by an Uncrewed Surface Vessel which caused a fire onboard. The crew have been rescued by local authorities and are safe and well. 
The vessel has been reported as sunk.
Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO while authorities are investigating.

UKMTO WARNING 106-26 ATTACK Report Date: 05 Aug 26 Report Time: 1430UTC
UKMTO has received a report of an incident 95NM southeast of Aden, Yemen. 
The Master of a tanker reported hearing a loud explosion in close proximity to the 
vessel. All crew accounted for and safe. There is no environmental impact reported.
Authorities are investigating. 
Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to 
UKMTO.

UKMTO has received a time late report of an incident 9NM southeast of Kumzar, Oman. The Master of a tanker has reported hearing two explosions whilst transiting in the Strait of Hormuz. 

The report confirms that crew and vessel are safe. No environmental damage has been reported.

Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO. 

UPDATE 001: UKMTO ATTACK Warning 107-26 has been reclassified to ADVISORY 107-26. After a review determined the intended target could not be conclusively identified.
Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO.

18/08/2026 ATTACK:
UKMTO has received a report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Company Security Officer has reported that the vessel was struck by an unknown projectile
while conducting an outbound transit of the Strait of Hormuz. The impact caused damage to the 
engine room and resulted in a crew casualty. The remaining crew are currently being assisted by 
the Omani Coast Guard.
At present, no environmental impact has been reported.

UKMTO has received a time late report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz.
A third party has reported that a bulk carrier was struck by an unknown projectile whilst conducting a transit of the Strait of Hormuz. The impact caused damage to the starboard side of 
the vessel and resulted in a crew casualty. 
There is no report of an environmental impact.
Authorities are investigating. Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO.

UKMTO WARNING 118-26 - HIJACK
Incident Date: 20 Aug 2026 Incident Time: TBC
UKMTO has received a report of an incident 136NM east of Al Mukalla, Yemen.

A tanker has broadcast a distress call on VHF 16 that they have been approached by an unauthorised vessel whilst travelling west in the Gulf of Aden.
Update 001 – UKMTO have received confirmation that the tanker has been boarded by six armed persons who are now in control of the vessel and redirecting to Somalia.
 
Authorities are investigating. 
Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO.
